go_around_training.what_is_it: A go-around is a rejected landing. You abort the approach and climb back to pattern altitude to try again. It's not a failure—it's a safety decision.
go_around_training.why_it_matters: Most landing accidents happen because pilots force a bad approach to touchdown. Go-arounds prevent crashes. You WILL get criticized for a rough landing, never for a go-around.

when_to_go_around.description: Airspeed not 65 KIAS ±5, altitude drifting, not centered on runway
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND immediately—don't chase it to the ground

when_to_go_around.description: Back pressure causes nose-up pitch, altitude increases suddenly
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND—you've lost control of descent

when_to_go_around.description: Main gear touches, then pops back up (porpoise)
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND on first bounce—don't try to salvage it

when_to_go_around.description: You're 15 feet AGL and haven't started flare yet
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND—you'll land hard, risk nose gear damage

when_to_go_around.description: Another aircraft on runway, debris, or animal
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND immediately—your safety is not negotiable

when_to_go_around.description: No specific problem, but approach feels unstable or unsafe
when_to_go_around.action: GO AROUND—trust your instinct, sort it out at altitude
GO AROUND, circle, build airspeed, try again from higher altitude

step_by_step.detail: Push throttle to 2,500 RPM—smooth, not aggressive
step_by_step.why: You need maximum power to climb against current drag (flaps extended, slow speed)
step_by_step.c172_specific: Throttle quadrant: move forward until stops
step_by_step.common_mistake: Half-power → insufficient climb performance, stall risk

step_by_step.detail: Push carb heat control in (full cold air)
step_by_step.why: Hot air = rich mixture = sluggish response. Cold air allows full power.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Carb heat knob on left side of panel, push OUT = ON, pull IN = OFF. Confusing. PUSH IN to shut it off.
step_by_step.common_mistake: Forget carb heat → lean mixture in cold weather → stumble → power loss

step_by_step.detail: Pull yoke back to arrest descent. Target: positive climb rate on VSI.
step_by_step.why: You're descending at 300-500 FPM. Need to stop that NOW. Then climb.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Initial pitch: approximately +5° nose-up attitude (slightly more up than level flight)
step_by_step.common_mistake: Wait for power to build → continue descending → closer to ground → less margin

step_by_step.detail: Check VSI: climbing (not descending). Check altimeter: increasing.
step_by_step.why: Don't touch flaps until you're SURE you're climbing. Premature flap retraction = sink.
step_by_step.common_mistake: Dump flaps at 50 AGL while still descending → sudden sink → stall

step_by_step.detail: Move flap lever from 30° to 20° position. Single notch up.
step_by_step.why: Reduces drag (allows faster climb). 20° still provides lift. Smooth transition.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Flap handle on left side of cockpit, between seats. Three positions: UP (0°), NOTCH (10°), DOWN (20°), FULL DOWN (30°). From final approach (30°), move to third-notch position (20°).
step_by_step.common_mistake: Retract to 0° too fast → loss of lift → sink

step_by_step.detail: Adjust pitch so airspeed indicator shows 74 KIAS. Use throttle for altitude, pitch for airspeed.
step_by_step.why: 74 KIAS = maximum rate of climb. Fastest way back to safety altitude.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Engine full power, carb heat off, pitch controls airspeed
step_by_step.common_mistake: Climb too slow (under 70 KIAS) → low margin above stall speed

step_by_step.detail: After 5-10 seconds of stable climb, move flap lever from 20° to 10°.
step_by_step.why: Reduce drag further. You're safe, airspeed increasing, altitude building.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Second notch down from full up
step_by_step.common_mistake: Too abrupt → pitch change → loss of airspeed control

step_by_step.detail: Once airspeed approaches 65-70 KIAS, move flap lever all the way up.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Flap lever all the way UP (fully retracted)
step_by_step.common_mistake: Flaps still down at pattern altitude → slower climb, unstable pattern

step_by_step.action: CONTINUE CLIMB TO PATTERN ALTITUDE (1,882 MSL)
step_by_step.detail: Maintain Vy (74 KIAS), level wings, continue climbing.
step_by_step.why: You need full altitude buffer before attempting approach again.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Pattern altitude for KHMP: 1,882 MSL (1,000 AGL). Don't level off early.
step_by_step.common_mistake: Level off at 1,500 MSL → unstable for another pattern

step_by_step.detail: Once at pattern altitude, turn to downwind. Announce: 'Minuteman traffic, Skyhawk 2177U, going around, left downwind Runway 24.'
step_by_step.why: Tells other traffic what you're doing. Smooth re-entry.
step_by_step.common_mistake: Tight, steep turn → lose airspeed → stall risk

step_by_step.detail: Level wings, trim for 90 KIAS, reduce power to 2,300 RPM, add flaps 10°.
step_by_step.why: You're back in the pattern. Reset for another approach.
step_by_step.c172_specific: Downwind profile: 1,882 MSL, 90 KIAS, flaps 10°, 2,300 RPM
step_by_step.common_mistake: Rush the setup → unstable again → another go-around

common_errors.consequence: Lean mixture at high power → engine stumble → loss of power when you need it most
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Carb heat OFF is step 2, do it IMMEDIATELY after full throttle. Make it automatic.

common_errors.consequence: Insufficient climb → stay low and slow → stall risk → panic
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Full throttle means 2,500 RPM. Smooth application, not jerky. But FULL.

common_errors.consequence: Lose lift → sink → descend instead of climb → crash
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Wait for positive climb rate confirmation (VSI shows +). Then 20°, then 10°, then 0°. Don't rush.

common_errors.consequence: Counterintuitive but it happens: student gets nervous, reduces throttle. Glide slope continues downward.
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Full power stays ON. Pitch up to arrest descent. Both together.

common_errors.error: Pitch Up Too Much Too Fast
common_errors.consequence: Rapid pitch change → airspeed bleeds → approach stall → panic
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Pitch up smoothly. Goal: Vy (74 KIAS) climb. Not nose-bleed angle of attack.

common_errors.consequence: Bank angle + slow speed = high stall speed. Over-bank = stall/spin risk.
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Keep turns shallow (<20° bank) while re-entering pattern. Wings level most of the time.

common_errors.consequence: Task saturation. Pilot fixates on poor flare while flying go-around → crashes into ground
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Aviate first. Analyze later. Right now: climb, re-enter pattern, focus on THIS approach.

common_errors.error: Flaps Still Extended at Pattern Altitude
common_errors.consequence: Slow climb = unstable entry = unstable approach = likely another go-around
common_errors.how_to_avoid: Follow steps exactly. By pattern altitude, flaps must be 0°.

breakdown.POWER: Full throttle, carb heat off (2,500 RPM)
breakdown.PITCH: Pull back to arrest descent (positive climb rate on VSI)
breakdown.CLIMB: Maintain Vy (74 KIAS) back to pattern altitude (1,882 MSL)
breakdown.REJOIN: Re-enter downwind, reset for another approach

callout.moment: When you commit to go-around (usually ~500 feet AGL or earlier if unstable)
callout.radio_call: Minuteman traffic, Skyhawk 2177 Uniform, going around, left downwind Runway 24
callout.why_announce: Other aircraft need to know you're not landing. Prevents conflicts in the pattern.
callout.cockpit_callout: Going around! [Throttle forward] Power! [Check] Carb heat! [Pull] Pitch up! [Check] Climbing!

criteria: Landing light visible 500-1,000 feet down runway
Too high (not descending) or too low (sinking fast)

training_emphasis.crawl_phase_focus: Decision to go around + power management + flap sequencing
training_emphasis.do_not_overthink: Aerodynamics, energy state, lift coefficient—save for post-flight debrief
training_emphasis.muscle_memory_goal: Student can execute POWER-PITCH-CLEAN-CLIMB-REJOIN without thinking
training_emphasis.by_solo: Student has performed ≥5 go-arounds, feels confident, no hesitation

safety_notes: Go-arounds are 100% normal. Best pilots perform them frequently.
Never criticize a student for going around. Praise the decision.
A go-around is easier to execute than a forced landing after a bad landing bounce.
In night flying or crosswind, lower the go-around threshold (try again sooner).
If you see a balloon forming (pitch increasing, altitude increasing), GO AROUND immediately. Don't wait for perfect clearance.
Forgetting carb heat is the #1 rookie mistake. Ingrain it: POWER → CARB HEAT OFF → PITCH.

common_questions.q: Will I get in trouble for going around?
common_questions.a: No. You'll get criticized for not going around when you should. Go-arounds are safe decisions. Forced bad landings are not.

common_questions.q: How many go-arounds can I do?
common_questions.a: As many as needed. At KHMP (non-towered), you control the pattern. Go around 10 times if needed to nail it.

common_questions.q: What if I forget a step?
common_questions.a: The critical sequence is POWER (full) → CARB HEAT OFF → PITCH UP. Everything else flows from that. Forget those three, and you're in trouble.

common_questions.q: What if the engine sputters when I apply full power?
common_questions.a: Carb heat OFF should fix it (cold air, richer mixture). If still rough, suspect carb ice—apply carb heat GENTLY, wait for power to build. If severe, land ASAP at nearest airport.

common_questions.q: Should I retract flaps all at once or gradually?
common_questions.a: GRADUALLY. 30° → 20° → 10° → 0°. Each step allows airspeed to stabilize before next step. Abrupt retraction = sink.

proficiency_standard.by_lesson_2: Student understands WHEN to go around and executes POWER-PITCH-CLEAN-CLIMB-REJOIN without major errors
proficiency_standard.by_lesson_4: Student can go around smoothly, flap sequence correct, re-enters pattern stably, ready for solo practice
proficiency_standard.by_private_pilot: Go-around is automatic—no hesitation, executed to ACS standards (altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kts, centered on runway)
